Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no skills. Factory code is department-agnostic and estate code names no specific loops.

OWNED FILES (only these; both new):
  factory/timersense.py
  tests/test_timersense.py

TASK: Build the estate timer sensor — the one deliberately non-deterministic edge that snapshots systemd user timers to JSON so downstream feed/board stay deterministic.

factory/timersense.py:
1. CLI: python3 -m factory.timersense --out <path> [--pattern <glob>]... — default out estate/state/timers.json relative to CWD; --pattern may repeat (fnmatch globs against unit names, e.g. '*loop*' '*-daily-*'); with no patterns, capture ALL user timers.
2. Collect via subprocess (systemctl --user): 'systemctl --user list-timers --all --no-pager --no-legend' parsed line-wise (columns: NEXT..LEFT..LAST..PASSED..UNIT ACTIVATES — parse robustly by splitting on the .timer/.service tokens, not fixed widths), then per matched service 'systemctl --user show <service> --property=ActiveState,SubState,Result,ExecMainStatus,ExecMainExitTimestamp,UnitFileState'. Inject the runner: a module-level _run(argv)->str via subprocess, monkeypatchable; tests NEVER call real systemctl.
3. Snapshot schema written atomically (temp+fsync+replace): {schema:'timers-snapshot/v1', captured_at: ISO-UTC, timers:[{unit, service, enabled: bool|'unknown', next_run: ISO|null, last_run: ISO|null, last_result: 'success'|'failure'|'unknown', exit_status: int|'unknown', group}]} where group = unit name with common suffixes stripped and prefix families kept (e.g. 'podcast-loop-guest-acquisition.timer' -> group 'podcast', 'seo-loop-daily.timer' -> 'seo', 'finance-os-daily-loop.timer' -> 'finance', 'social-escalations.timer' -> 'social', anything unmatched -> 'other') — implement as first-dash-segment heuristic with a small explicit override map argument, never hardcoding a full loop list.
4. Honesty: any field systemctl does not yield is 'unknown'/null, never fabricated; systemctl absent or erroring -> exit 1 with a clear message, and with --tolerate-missing write a valid snapshot with timers: [] and note:'systemctl unavailable'.
5. Timestamps normalized to ISO UTC (parse systemd's 'Day YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ' format; unparseable -> null). Logging module only; stdout prints one JSON receipt {timers, groups, out}.

tests/test_timersense.py — at least 8 tests, all with a monkeypatched _run returning fixture strings: list-timers parsing yields units+next/last; show parsing yields enabled/result/exit; failure Result maps to 'failure'; unparseable timestamp -> null not crash; grouping heuristic (podcast-loop-*, seo-loop-*, social-*, unmatched->other); pattern filtering; --tolerate-missing writes empty valid snapshot; atomic write leaves valid JSON; receipt shape.

VERIFY: 'python3 loopfactory.py check' full suite green. You fail for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 8 new 'def test_' functions, or the verify command failing.
tasks.verified: systemd user timers snapshot to a deterministic JSON contract with honest unknowns, injectable runner, and grouping

tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no skills. Factory code names no specific loops or departments.

OWNED FILES (only these; the test file and systemd templates are new):
  factory/boardfeed.py
  factory/board.py
  templates/systemd/estate-board.service
  templates/systemd/estate-board.timer
  templates/department_daily.sh.template
  tests/test_allloops_board.py

CONTEXT: factory/boardfeed.py aggregates loop-factory departments into board-feed.ndjson; factory/board.py renders Board Template v1 (read both fully). A parallel task is creating factory/timersense.py which writes estate/state/timers.json with schema {schema:'timers-snapshot/v1', captured_at, timers:[{unit, service, enabled, next_run, last_run, last_result: success|failure|unknown, exit_status, group}]} — do NOT import or create that module; consume ONLY the JSON file per this schema (build fixtures by hand).

CHANGES:
1. factory/boardfeed.py — build_feed gains optional timers_path (default: <repo_root>/estate/state/timers.json, tolerated absent). When present and valid: for each timer emit kind 'loop_status', department = its 'group', id 'loop_status:<group>:<unit>:<hour-bucket of captured_at>', data {unit, service, enabled, next_run, last_run, last_result, exit_status}. ADDITIONALLY: a timer with last_result 'failure' emits an andon line {code:'LOOP_FAILED', severity:'breach', detail:'<unit> last run failed (exit <status>)', observed:'failure', setpoint:'success'}; a timer whose next_run is null AND enabled is not True emits nothing extra (disabled units are shown, not alarmed). Malformed/mis-schema'd timers.json counts into feed_health malformed, never crashes. Keep determinism (sort as today) and update the receipt to include 'loops': count.
2. factory/board.py — render loop_status rows as a new 'All loops' subsection at the END of Zone 3 Activity: grouped by department/group, one row per unit — status dot (green last_result success, red failure, muted unknown), unit name (strip .timer), last run, next run, 'disabled' tag when enabled is false; rows with unknowns render the word unknown. Keep the existing andon pipeline untouched so LOOP_FAILED andons appear in Zone 2 automatically. Empty/missing loop data -> the subsection shows 'no loop telemetry — run timersense'.
3. templates/systemd/estate-board.service + .timer — a user service running, from the repo root: python3 -m factory.timersense --out estate/state/timers.json --tolerate-missing, then python3 -m factory.boardfeed --repo-root ., then the two factory.board renders (estate board.html + no department filter). Use Type=oneshot with ExecStart lines or a bash -c chain; timer OnCalendar=*:0/15 (every 15 min), Persistent=true. HEADER COMMENT in both files (copy the discipline from the existing templates/systemd/ files — read them): installed DISABLED, owner enables deliberately, shadow-safe (read-only sensing + local HTML writes only).
4. templates/department_daily.sh.template — in the board step, add the timersense call before boardfeed so scaffolded departments refresh loop telemetry too.

tests/test_allloops_board.py — at least 9 tests using tmp fixtures: loop_status rows emitted from a fixture timers.json; grouping lands rows under their group department; failure timer -> LOOP_FAILED andon present AND loop_status row present; disabled timer shows enabled false with no andon; absent timers.json -> no loop rows, no crash, receipt loops=0; malformed timers.json counted in feed_health; renderer shows the All loops subsection with unit rows and status dots (parse HTML text); renderer empty-state message when no loop rows; determinism (two builds byte-identical with same fixture); Zone 2 shows the LOOP_FAILED andon content.

VERIFY: 'python3 loopfactory.py check' full suite green. You fail for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 9 new 'def test_' functions, or the verify command failing.
tasks.verified: every systemd loop on the box appears on the one board with health dots, failed loops raise andons, and a 15-minute refresh timer ships installed-disabled
